sources.title: Paul Ekman Group: Facial Action Coding System
sources.supports: FACS describes visually discernible facial actions; action description and emotion inference are separate.
sources.limits: The paid 2002 manual was not acquired; this research is not certified FACS coding.

sources.title: CMU facial expression laboratory: FACS reference
sources.supports: Names of the 22 AU identifiers in the source inventory.
sources.limits: The page labels its reference as 1978; not a replacement for current manual criteria or intensity coding.

sources.title: OpenFace developer documentation: Action Units
sources.supports: Supported AU subset; presence/intensity differences; image and person-normalized sequence limitations.
sources.limits: No software inference was run; a model score is not a sufficient render gate.

sources.title: Barrett et al. 2019: Emotional Expressions Reconsidered
sources.supports: Facial movements do not uniquely identify an emotion across people, situations and cultures.
sources.limits: Does not supply a universal replacement emotion-to-face recipe.

sources.title: Cowen and Keltner 2017: Self-report captures 27 categories of emotion bridged by continuous gradients
sources.supports: Affective experience can contain many categories and continuous transitions.
sources.limits: Self-report under the study protocol; not proof of 27 fixed faces or the reference's 32 families.

sources.title: Martin et al. 2021: Evidence for Distinct Facial Signals of Reward, Affiliation, and Dominance from Both Perception and Production Tasks
sources.supports: Reward, affiliation and dominance functions; visible smile form, function and authenticity are distinct.
sources.limits: A depicted configuration does not establish sincerity, disposition or consent.

sources.title: Orlowska et al. 2018: Dynamics Matter: Recognition of Reward, Affiliative, and Dominance Smiles From Dynamic vs. Static Displays
sources.supports: Static and dynamic smile evidence are different experimental conditions; the observed dynamic advantage was significant for affiliative smiles.
sources.limits: Study-specific recognition results do not validate a generated image.

sources.title: Yan et al. 2014: CASME II
sources.supports: Microexpression annotations involve temporal onset, apex and offset.
sources.limits: Paper read only; no dataset download, license approval, training or lie-detection claim.

sources.title: Aviezer et al. 2012: Body cues, not facial expressions, discriminate between intense positive and negative emotions
sources.supports: Body and situation can affect interpretation of intense expressions.
sources.limits: Controlled experiment; not a universal body-language decoder.

sources.title: Peter Hurley: Squinch
sources.supports: Portrait instruction emphasizes raising the lower eyelid, with a narrower visible eye opening.
sources.limits: A posing practice, not a guaranteed confidence signal or certified AU equivalence.

sources.title: Collins: smize
sources.supports: Informal eye-focused smiling term.
sources.limits: No uniquely specified muscle combination.

sources.title: Merriam-Webster: smirk
sources.supports: Self-satisfied or condescending smile; asymmetry is not a necessary definition.
sources.limits: Dictionary meaning only; the visual decomposition in this package is an authored proposal.

sources.title: Wiktionary: o-face
sources.supports: Explicit sexual reference category, distinct from general flirting or an open mouth.
sources.limits: Lexical classification only; no explicit render recipe or candidate proposal.

sources.title: Wiktionary: ahegao

sources.limits: Lexical classification only; no explicit render recipe or candidate proposal.

sources.title: RADA: Focus on acting technique
sources.supports: Technique organizes action and scene work rather than one compulsory facial expression.
sources.limits: No universal acting-method-to-AU mapping.

sources.title: RADA: Stanislavski workshop
sources.supports: Given circumstances, objectives and action are useful scene-design concepts.
sources.limits: Course description, not a complete manual or result verification.

sources.title: Neighborhood Playhouse: Two-year conservatory
sources.supports: Meisner-oriented training concerns responsive scene practice.
sources.limits: Do not serialize an approach name as a fixed facial movement.

sources.title: Lee Strasberg Institute: What is Method Acting?
sources.supports: Method and memory-based actor preparation belong to method metadata.
sources.limits: Not evidence of depicted internal memory or emotion.

sources.title: HB Studio: The Uta approach
sources.supports: Actor preparation and circumstances can inform authored scene tasks.
sources.limits: No method label should impose appearance or identity.

sources.title: Stella Adler Studio: Acting Technique 1
sources.supports: Imagination and scene circumstances are preparation concepts.
sources.limits: Training metadata, not a mandatory pose.

sources.title: Michael Chekhov Association
sources.supports: Movement and imagination are aspects of the approach.
sources.limits: Do not claim a standardized gesture-to-emotion conversion from the homepage.

sources.title: University of Maryland: Laban theory
sources.supports: Effort axes include time, weight, space and flow.
sources.limits: A still posture cannot demonstrate effort history or measured force.

sources.title: ASHA: Voice disorders practice portal
sources.supports: Pitch, loudness and voice quality are different acoustic descriptions.
sources.limits: Vocabulary only; no diagnosis, audio test or inference from a face.

sources.title: SAG-AFTRA: Intimacy coordinator resources
sources.supports: Production choreography, boundaries and consent are distinct from portrayed attraction.
sources.limits: No claim that facial expression establishes consent; no new product approval flow.
